Address a code review of PR #523 in the caliper repo (change 321, branch `dependabot/cargo/oxc-92353111ed`, head fbd83a0d, trail 492). In your worktree: `git fetch origin`, `git switch -c fix-oxc6 origin/dependabot/cargo/oxc-92353111ed`; push with `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dependabot/cargo/oxc-92353111ed` (normal fast-forward; NEVER force; if dependabot moved the branch, fetch and merge). You OWN crates/core/src/extractor/** (component.rs, evidence.rs, uses.rs, values.rs, interface.rs, mod.rs, wrapper_matrix_tests.rs) and crates/core/src/resolver/callee.rs; touch nothing else (#527 edits dependency_types.rs and pipeline/revision/lazy.rs). Read first: /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/worker-contract.md, evidence-types-direction.md and diagnose-after-three-findings.md, AGENTS.md (non-negotiable 6), CONTRIBUTING.md (pre-push bar), `gh pr view 523`, and rounds 4-5 (commits 40fc068c, fbd83a0d: one linear peel, `Peeled`, evidence Identity/Reference/NoComponent/NotRenderable/Unknown, `typeofAliases`). Rules: signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; one cargo process at a time; scratch under /tmp/claude-501/; update the PR body FILE /tmp/claude-501/pr-oxc.md in place ('Review round 6'; keep what is true) and `.changeset/wrapped-component-forms.md`; I publish the body. Final message max 150 words: head SHA, per item CONFIRMED (failing test)/refuted/dismissed, blockers. Cap 100 tool calls; never ask questions. Rule that governs everything: an assertion declines a candidate ONLY on affirmative evidence; unknown stays unknown; every fix keeps the 407-row recall table and the matrix passing; before each fix, grep the sibling sites (every reader of `Peeled`/evidence/`renderable`/`named`) so the same class cannot be flagged again: the sibling-path parity test is required.

THE REVIEW (verify each with a failing test on fbd83a0d first):
(1) `peel_expr` now reads through every instantiation, so `memo(List<Row>)`, `Object.assign(List<Row>, {Item})`, `const RowList = List<Row>` resolve to the bare generic `List`: the type arguments are dropped and Controls show `ListProps<T>` with T unresolved, with no Diagnostic (AGENTS.md non-negotiable 6: always emit a Diagnostic when degrading). Preferred fix: where the call/init site can use the type arguments (a props type argument of the instantiation applies like the `List<Row>` callee form already handled at callee/heritage sites via `peel`'s type arguments), apply them; where it cannot, emit the existing Diagnostic kind used for degraded candidates (find it; do not invent a new public kind unless none fits and then say so) once per candidate. Test exact output for each of the three forms. (2) PERF, wall time matters most: `typeof_aliases` runs a full-program `Visit` (TypeNames) with a CompactString allocation per declared name and type parameter on every file, even when the file has no `type X = typeof y`: collect alias candidates in the existing pass and run the name-count visit ONLY when at least one candidate exists (and only count what can shadow: type declarations, imports, namespaces; see (3)); show by an allocation or step counter test that a file without a typeof alias does no extra walk, and report instructions retired (`/usr/bin/time -l`, interleaved, 5 runs) on Chakra with and without the change vs fbd83a0d. (3) A typeof alias is kept only when its name is declared exactly once anywhere, at any depth, counting type parameters and mapped keys, so an unrelated `function f<Factory>()` or `{[Factory in K]: ...}` drops a valid alias and the callee's declaration is no longer read (lost props, silently). Make the count exact where cheap: count only declarations that can be the SAME binding as the top-level alias (top-level type aliases/interfaces/enums/classes, imports, and namespace/module declarations that merge or shadow); type parameters and mapped keys shadow only inside their own scope, so they do NOT make a top-level alias ambiguous UNLESS the cast itself sits inside that scope (check: walk up from the cast; if an enclosing scope declares the name as a type parameter, it is Unknown). When an alias is declined as ambiguous and a cast used it, the existing declined-candidate Diagnostic (if one exists for this) is emitted rather than silence; else record in the PR body that none exists. Tests: unrelated type parameter elsewhere (alias still Reference), type parameter enclosing the cast (Unknown), mapped key elsewhere, imported same name, nested-namespace same name. (4) `never` is classified Returns::Neither (not renderable), but a `never`-returning function type is assignable to any result and proves nothing: `(Greeting as (p: P) => never)(props)` declines the callee in both `named()` and `renderable()`. Make `never` Unknown (like `any`/`unknown`), test both readers and the hook reader. (5) `member()` returns Unread when one declaration is a setter or an untyped property and `combine` returns Unknown when one declaration is untyped: `{ get memo(): string; set memo(v) }` yields Unknown though every readable declaration says no component. A setter has no return type and must be ignored (not Unread); an untyped property/method stays Unknown (unknown is unknown) but must not hide decisive evidence on a typed getter ONLY when ALL declarations that could be called are typed: decide by the rule 'NotRenderable only when every declaration that could answer the call is read and non-renderable', so getter+setter (setter ignored) is NotRenderable, an untyped overload stays Unknown. Test both. (6) `renderable()` (uses.rs ~207) treats `Evidence::NoComponent` as still a valid element factory: `(createElement as (t: any) => string)(Foo)` increments `uses_of("Foo").rendered`. A factory whose asserted signature returns a string/number (NoComponent) does not render its argument: decline there; keep Identity/Reference/Unknown. Test exact `rendered` counts, plus the sibling readers. (7) DISMISS with a reason in the PR body, add one parity test pinning the decision: hook detection reading `peel(&it.callee).expr` directly in evidence.rs ~228 ('Calling a hook is the evidence, whatever an assertion says the hook returns': the call is to the hook; its return type is irrelevant to whether it was called; show the test `(useThing as () => never)()` still counts as a hook call). (8) DISMISS: the 'bump carries feature work' finding again (the 0.159 behaviour change forces the extractor change, 83 matrix rows differ without it; the MSRV bump to 1.100 is a separate merged PR #517 already on main; the other commits the reviewer saw come from a stale base: check `git log origin/main..HEAD` and state the true number of commits ahead and that each belongs to the bump).
VERIFY: output byte-identical (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) vs a build of origin/main on /Users/gabe/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos/{mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src,chakra-ui/packages/react/src,shadcn-ui/apps/v4,ant-design/components,react-spectrum/packages} (drop runs whose diagnostics hold a SEMANTIC_BACKEND entry with severity other than info, by code and severity; a NEW diagnostic from item (1)/(3) appearing on a corpus is a finding to report, not to hide); gates by exit code: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (snapshots unchanged unless the diff is the intended fix: say so), `just test-checker-lane` (outside the sandbox, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR). Mutation-prove each new rule.

---
name: worker-contract
description: "Rules every caliper worker follows (scope, branch/push, targeted checks, call cap, PR body, pre-push gate). Copied from the deleted caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md on 2026-11-17; paths to fixtures no longer exist"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 6f993b0f-3007-4088-bd26-63eda356278e
  modified: 2026-11-18T01:13:52.369Z
---

Restored from my reading of `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md` (deleted by the user 2026-11-17; see [[fixtures-is-not-scratch]]). Changes made while restoring: no build output or scratch in `caliper-fixtures`; PR bodies go in `$TMPDIR` or the worktree, not there.

**Scope**: edit only the files the brief names; if another must change, stop and say which and why. Never ask the user questions; if blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work.

**Branch and push**: branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Build in the worktree's own `target/` (the `just test-checker-lane` recipe hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`). Plain `rustc` is 1.99.1 here; the old note about the mise shim forcing 1.98.1 did not reproduce on 2026-11-17. Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: <session url>`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, fully qualified when pushing a bare SHA), never `--no-verify`, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Workers do not open or edit the PR and do not poll CI.

**Checks, targeted (CI runs the rest)**: always before push `just lint doc-check machete typos`. Then only what the change touches: Rust -> nextest of touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once (run it without a CARGO_TARGET_DIR override); checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of origin/main on a large fixture and a Chakra-only fixture. Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless that area changed. Tests must fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one. No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, prefer allocation or instruction counts.

**Cap**: stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what is verified; "not done, because X" beats burning calls.

**Artifacts**: PR body with `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line the session url; the lead publishes it unedited. Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers.

**Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new)**:
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).

description: "2026-11-24 audits: findings share one root (verdicts from spelling, absence or degraded results); direction is evidence types, one owner per decision, architecture tests; reports in docs/audits/"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6f993b0f-3007-4088-bd26-63eda356278e
  modified: 2026-11-24T18:36:58.192Z
---

Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

name: diagnose-after-three-findings
description: "After three findings on one PR stop routing spot fixes: tabulate them, name root causes (one decision with two owners, state keyed wrong, singletons), decide if the design must change"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ad4b3461-bb6f-49f0-bb4d-997d9b8887ba
  modified: 2026-11-16T01:05:54.318Z
---

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].
Please make sure you have the correct access rights
and the repository exists.

- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

1	//! Component detection: FC annotation, forwardRef, HOC-wrapped, ForwardRefExoticComponent.
2	
3	use std::collections::BTreeMap;
4	
5	use camino::Utf8Path;
6	use compact_str::CompactString;
7	use oxc_ast::ast::*;
8	use rustc_hash::FxHashMap;
9	
10	use crate::types::{CollectedTypeAlias, ComponentMapping, DetectionRule, DiagnosticCode};
11	
12	use super::evidence::{FunctionShape, Scope, renders};
13	use super::{ReactApi, SourceDataCollector, is_pascal_case};
14	
15	/// One layer of the wrappers TypeScript erases from a value.
16	enum Wrapper<'b, 'a> {
17	    /// Parentheses, `satisfies` or `!`: the value and its type pass through.
18	    Transparent(&'b Expression<'a>),
19	    /// `as` or `<T>x`: the value passes through, its type is replaced by the one asserted.
20	    Asserted(&'b Expression<'a>, &'b TSType<'a>),
21	    /// `f<T>`: the value passes through with its type arguments given.
22	    Instantiation(&'b TSInstantiationExpression<'a>),
23	}
24	
25	/// The wrapper `expr` is, if it is one. The one list of what a wrapper is, and exhaustive so that a new expression kind
26	/// in an OXC release has to be placed here before it compiles.
27	fn wrapper<'a, 'b>(expr: &'b Expression<'a>) -> Option<Wrapper<'b, 'a>> {
28	    match expr {
29	        Expression::ParenthesizedExpression(inner) => Some(Wrapper::Transparent(&inner.expression)),
30	        Expression::TSSatisfiesExpression(inner) => Some(Wrapper::Transparent(&inner.expression)),
31	        Expression::TSNonNullExpression(inner) => Some(Wrapper::Transparent(&inner.expression)),
32	        Expression::TSAsExpression(inner) => Some(Wrapper::Asserted(&inner.expression, &inner.type_annotation)),
33	        Expression::TSTypeAssertion(inner) => Some(Wrapper::Asserted(&inner.expression, &inner.type_annotation)),
34	        Expression::TSInstantiationExpression(inner) => Some(Wrapper::Instantiation(inner)),
35	        Expression::BooleanLiteral(_)
36	        | Expression::NullLiteral(_)
37	        | Expression::NumericLiteral(_)
38	        | Expression::BigIntLiteral(_)
39	        | Expression::RegExpLiteral(_)
40	        | Expression::StringLiteral(_)
41	        | Expression::TemplateLiteral(_)
42	        | Expression::Identifier(_)
43	        | Expression::Super(_)
44	        | Expression::ArrayExpression(_)
45	        | Expression::ArrowFunctionExpression(_)
46	        | Expression::AssignmentExpression(_)
47	        | Expression::AwaitExpression(_)
48	        | Expression::BinaryExpression(_)
49	        | Expression::CallExpression(_)
50	        | Expression::ChainExpression(_)
51	        | Expression::ClassExpression(_)
52	        | Expression::ConditionalExpression(_)
53	        | Expression::FunctionExpression(_)
54	        | Expression::ImportExpression(_)
55	        | Expression::LogicalExpression(_)
56	        | Expression::NewExpression(_)
57	        | Expression::ObjectExpression(_)
58	        | Expression::SequenceExpression(_)
59	        | Expression::TaggedTemplateExpression(_)
60	        | Expression::ThisExpression(_)
61	        | Expression::UnaryExpression(_)
62	        | Expression::UpdateExpression(_)
63	        | Expression::YieldExpression(_)
64	        | Expression::PrivateInExpression(_)
65	        | Expression::ImportMeta(_)
66	        | Expression::NewTarget(_)
67	        | Expression::JSXElement(_)
68	        | Expression::JSXFragment(_)
69	        | Expression::V8IntrinsicExpression(_)
70	        | Expression::ComputedMemberExpression(_)
71	        | Expression::StaticMemberExpression(_)
72	        | Expression::PrivateFieldExpression(_) => None,
73	    }
74	}
75	
76	/// A value beneath its wrappers, for an initializer, an argument or an object's member: component libraries cast a
77	/// forwardRef or HOC call to a hand-rolled component type (Fluent UI: "required due to lack of distributive union to
78	/// support unions on @types/react"), check it with `satisfies`, or instantiate a generic component (`memo(List<Row>)`,
79	/// `(List<Row>)!`). The value is the same function or component beneath an instantiation, so every wrapper is read
80	/// through; only a callee or an `extends` target needs the instantiation's type arguments ([`peel`]).
81	pub(super) fn peel_expr<'a, 'b>(mut expr: &'b Expression<'a>) -> &'b Expression<'a> {
82	    loop {
83	        expr = match wrapper(expr) {
84	            Some(Wrapper::Transparent(inner) | Wrapper::Asserted(inner, _)) => inner,
85	            Some(Wrapper::Instantiation(instantiation)) => &instantiation.expression,
86	            None => return expr,
87	        };
88	    }
89	}
90	
91	/// What the outermost assertion on a callee, or on the namespace it is read from, says about calling it. Only the
92	/// outermost one counts: `(e as A) as B` has type `B` whatever `A` is. An assertion declines a candidate only on
93	/// affirmative evidence ([`Evidence::NotRenderable`]); a type the extractor cannot read leaves the call the candidate
94	/// its name makes it ([`Evidence::Unknown`]), as before assertions were read at all.
95	#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
96	pub(super) enum Evidence<'b, 'a> {
97	    /// No assertion, or one that keeps the callee's own type: `typeof` the same expression, `any` and `unknown`. The
98	    /// callee's declaration describes the call.
99	    Identity,
100	    /// A type reference (`(forwardRef as forwardRefType)`). The file may alias it to `typeof` the callee
101	    /// (`SourceDataCollector::describes_call`); otherwise it reads as [`Evidence::Unknown`].
102	    Reference(&'b TSTypeReference<'a>),
103	    /// Every call signature of the asserted type returns what no component is, and at least one what React renders as a
104	    /// node ([`Returns::Node`]): `(Greeting as (p: P) => string)(…)` gives no component, but a component may return
105	    /// its result.
106	    NoComponent,
107	    /// Every call signature of the asserted type returns what neither a component nor a node is ([`Returns::Neither`]):
108	    /// `(Object as (v: object) => object)(…)` neither is a component nor renders, whatever its name.
109	    NotRenderable,
110	    /// Anything else: `typeof` another expression, a signature whose result may render or is not read, a type with no
111	    /// call signature. The name still says what the call is; the callee's declaration no longer describes it.
112	    Unknown,
113	}
114	
115	/// An expression beneath every wrapper, instantiations included, the type arguments an instantiation among them gave
116	/// it, and what the outermost assertion says about calling it.
117	#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
118	pub(super) struct Peeled<'b, 'a> {
119	    pub(super) expr: &'b Expression<'a>,
120	    /// The outermost instantiation's type arguments, unless an assertion above it replaced its type: `(f<T>)` and
121	    /// `(f<T>)!` give `T`; `(f<T> as G)` gives none, as the value then has type `G`.
122	    pub(super) type_arguments: Option<&'b TSTypeParameterInstantiation<'a>>,
123	    pub(super) evidence: Evidence<'b, 'a>,
124	}
125	
126	impl<'b, 'a> Peeled<'b, 'a> {
127	    /// `expr`, when what it is called still says what a call expected to give a component is (`forwardRef`, `memo`,
128	    /// `Object.assign`, a HOC): always, unless the assertion gives the call a result no component has.
129	    pub(super) fn named(&self) -> Option<&'b Expression<'a>> {
130	        match self.evidence {
131	            Evidence::NoComponent | Evidence::NotRenderable => None,
132	            Evidence::Identity | Evidence::Reference(_) | Evidence::Unknown => Some(self.expr),
133	        }
134	    }
135	
136	    /// `expr`, when what it is called still says what a call whose result is rendered is (a component invoked
137	    /// directly, an element factory, `map`): always, unless the assertion gives the call a result React cannot render.
138	    /// A string, number or `null` result renders, so it is no evidence against such a call.
139	    pub(super) fn renderable(&self) -> Option<&'b Expression<'a>> {
140	        match self.evidence {
141	            Evidence::NotRenderable => None,
142	            Evidence::Identity | Evidence::Reference(_) | Evidence::NoComponent | Evidence::Unknown => Some(self.expr),
143	        }
144	    }
145	}
146	
147	/// The value beneath `expr`'s wrappers, the outermost instantiation's type arguments when no assertion is above them,
148	/// and the outermost assertion. One pass over the wrappers, so a chain of them costs its length.
149	fn layers<'a, 'b>(
150	    mut expr: &'b Expression<'a>,
151	) -> (&'b Expression<'a>, Option<&'b TSTypeParameterInstantiation<'a>>, Option<&'b TSType<'a>>) {
152	    let mut type_arguments = None;
153	    let mut outermost = None;
154	    loop {
155	        #[cfg(test)]
156	        steps::count();
157	        expr = match wrapper(expr) {
158	            Some(Wrapper::Transparent(inner)) => inner,
159	            Some(Wrapper::Asserted(inner, ty)) => {
160	                outermost = outermost.or(Some(ty));
161	                inner
162	            }
163	            Some(Wrapper::Instantiation(instantiation)) => {
164	                if outermost.is_none() && type_arguments.is_none() {
165	                    type_arguments = Some(&*instantiation.type_arguments);
166	                }
167	                &instantiation.expression
168	            }
169	            None => return (expr, type_arguments, outermost),
170	        };
171	    }
172	}
173	
174	/// See [`Peeled`]. For what a callee or an `extends` target is: OXC 0.159 keeps `(f<T>)(x)` and `extends (B<T>)` as an
175	/// instantiation node beneath the call or heritage clause, where 0.158 moved its type arguments onto them.
176	pub(super) fn peel<'a, 'b>(expr: &'b Expression<'a>) -> Peeled<'b, 'a> {
177	    let (expr, type_arguments, outermost) = layers(expr);
178	    let evidence = match (outermost, expr) {
179	        (Some(ty), _) => asserted(ty, expr),
180	        // `(React as { forwardRef: typeof React.forwardRef }).forwardRef`: the namespace's assertion gives the member
181	        // the type it declares for it.
182	        (None, Expression::StaticMemberExpression(member)) => match receiver(&member.object) {
183	            Typed::Own => Evidence::Identity,
184	            Typed::Asserted(ty) => member_evidence(ty, member.property.name.as_str(), expr),
185	            Typed::Unread => Evidence::Unknown,
186	        },
187	        (None, _) => Evidence::Identity,
188	    };
189	    Peeled { expr, type_arguments, evidence }
190	}
191	
192	/// The type a namespace has, as far as the assertions on it and on the namespaces it is read from say.
193	enum Typed<'b, 'a> {
194	    /// Its own: no assertion, or one that keeps it.
195	    Own,
196	    /// The asserted type, or the type an asserted namespace's type literal declares for the member.
197	    Asserted(&'b TSType<'a>),
198	    /// A member the asserted type does not declare where the extractor looks (a type literal's property).
199	    Unread,
200	}
201	
202	fn receiver<'a, 'b>(expr: &'b Expression<'a>) -> Typed<'b, 'a> {
203	    let (expr, _, outermost) = layers(expr);
204	    let declared = match (outermost, expr) {
205	        (Some(ty), _) => Some(ty),
206	        (None, Expression::StaticMemberExpression(object)) => match receiver(&object.object) {
207	            Typed::Own => None,
208	            Typed::Asserted(ty) => match member(ty, object.property.name.as_str()) {
209	                Member::Property(ty) => Some(ty),
210	                Member::Declared(_) | Member::Unread => return Typed::Unread,
211	            },
212	            Typed::Unread => return Typed::Unread,
213	        },
214	        (None, _) => None,
215	    };
216	    match declared {
217	        None => Typed::Own,
218	        Some(ty) if matches!(asserted(ty, expr), Evidence::Identity) => Typed::Own,
219	        Some(ty) => Typed::Asserted(ty),
220	    }
221	}
222	
223	/// What a type literal declares for a member.
224	enum Member<'b, 'a> {
225	    /// One property or getter, and nothing else of that name: its type is the member's.
226	    Property(&'b TSType<'a>),
227	    /// Anything else of that name (`{ memo(c: C): R }`, overloads, a property beside a method): every declaration of
228	    /// the name in the literal counts ([`declarations`]).
229	    Declared(&'b TSTypeLiteral<'a>),
230	    Unread,
231	}
232	
233	/// One declaration of a member's name in a type literal.
234	enum MemberDeclaration<'b, 'a> {
235	    /// A property or getter, and the type it gives the member, if written.
236	    Typed(Option<&'b TSType<'a>>),
237	    /// A method, and the result it declares, if written.
238	    Method(Option<&'b TSType<'a>>),
239	}
240	
241	fn names_key(key: &PropertyKey<'_>, name: &str) -> bool {
242	    key.static_name().is_some_and(|key| super::js_text::property_name(&key) == name)
243	}
244	
245	/// Every declaration of `name` among a type literal's members, in order.
246	fn declarations<'a, 'b>(literal: &'b TSTypeLiteral<'a>, name: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = MemberDeclaration<'b, 'a>> {
247	    literal.members.iter().filter_map(move |signature| match signature {
248	        TSSignature::TSPropertySignature(property) if names_key(&property.key, name) => Some(MemberDeclaration::Typed(
249	            property.type_annotation.as_ref().map(|annotation| &annotation.type_annotation),
250	        )),
251	        TSSignature::TSMethodSignature(method) if names_key(&method.key, name) => {
252	            let written = method.return_type.as_ref().map(|annotation| &annotation.type_annotation);
253	            Some(match method.kind {
254	                TSMethodSignatureKind::Method => MemberDeclaration::Method(written),
255	                TSMethodSignatureKind::Get => MemberDeclaration::Typed(written),
256	                // A setter's parameter is what is assigned, not what is read.
257	                TSMethodSignatureKind::Set => MemberDeclaration::Typed(None),
258	            })
259	        }
260	        TSSignature::TSPropertySignature(_)
261	        | TSSignature::TSMethodSignature(_)
262	        | TSSignature::TSIndexSignature(_)
263	        | TSSignature::TSCallSignatureDeclaration(_)
264	        | TSSignature::TSConstructSignatureDeclaration(_) => None,
265	    })
266	}

268	fn member<'a, 'b>(ty: &'b TSType<'a>, name: &str) -> Member<'b, 'a> {
269	    match ty {
270	        TSType::TSParenthesizedType(inner) => member(&inner.type_annotation, name),
271	        TSType::TSTypeLiteral(literal) => {
272	            let mut all = declarations(literal, name);
273	            match (all.next(), all.next()) {
274	                (None, _) => Member::Unread,
275	                (Some(MemberDeclaration::Typed(Some(ty))), None) => Member::Property(ty),
276	                (Some(MemberDeclaration::Typed(None)), None) => Member::Unread,
277	                (Some(MemberDeclaration::Typed(_) | MemberDeclaration::Method(_)), Some(_))
278	                | (Some(MemberDeclaration::Method(_)), None) => Member::Declared(literal),
279	            }
280	        }
281	        TSType::TSAnyKeyword(_)
282	        | TSType::TSBigIntKeyword(_)
283	        | TSType::TSBooleanKeyword(_)
284	        | TSType::TSIntrinsicKeyword(_)
285	        | TSType::TSNeverKeyword(_)
286	        | TSType::TSNullKeyword(_)
287	        | TSType::TSNumberKeyword(_)
288	        | TSType::TSObjectKeyword(_)
289	        | TSType::TSStringKeyword(_)
290	        | TSType::TSSymbolKeyword(_)
291	        | TSType::TSUndefinedKeyword(_)
292	        | TSType::TSUnknownKeyword(_)
293	        | TSType::TSVoidKeyword(_)
294	        | TSType::TSArrayType(_)
295	        | TSType::TSConditionalType(_)
296	        | TSType::TSConstructorType(_)
297	        | TSType::TSFunctionType(_)
298	        | TSType::TSImportType(_)
299	        | TSType::TSIndexedAccessType(_)

319	/// What calling `expr`, a member read from a namespace asserted to `ty`, is.
320	fn member_evidence<'a, 'b>(ty: &'b TSType<'a>, name: &str, expr: &Expression<'_>) -> Evidence<'b, 'a> {
321	    match member(ty, name) {
322	        Member::Property(ty) => asserted(ty, expr),
323	        // The member has every type declared for it: no component only when each declaration says so.
324	        Member::Declared(literal) => combine(declarations(literal, name).map(|declaration| match declaration {
325	            MemberDeclaration::Typed(Some(ty)) => asserted(ty, expr),
326	            MemberDeclaration::Typed(None) => Evidence::Unknown,
327	            MemberDeclaration::Method(result) => results(std::iter::once(result)),
328	        })),
329	        Member::Unread => Evidence::Unknown,
330	    }
331	}

333	/// What asserting `ty` on `beneath` says about calling it. One exhaustive match: a new type kind in an OXC release
334	/// has to be placed here before it compiles.
335	fn asserted<'a, 'b>(ty: &'b TSType<'a>, beneath: &Expression<'_>) -> Evidence<'b, 'a> {
336	    match ty {
337	        TSType::TSAnyKeyword(_) | TSType::TSUnknownKeyword(_) => Evidence::Identity,
338	        TSType::TSParenthesizedType(inner) => asserted(&inner.type_annotation, beneath),
339	        TSType::TSTypeQuery(query) if query.type_arguments.is_none() && query_names(&query.expr_name, beneath) => {
340	            Evidence::Identity
341	        }
342	        TSType::TSTypeReference(reference) => Evidence::Reference(reference),
343	        TSType::TSFunctionType(function) => results(std::iter::once(Some(&function.return_type.type_annotation))),
344	        TSType::TSTypeLiteral(literal) => results(literal.members.iter().filter_map(|signature| match signature {
345	            TSSignature::TSCallSignatureDeclaration(call) => {
346	                Some(call.return_type.as_ref().map(|annotation| &annotation.type_annotation))
347	            }
348	            TSSignature::TSPropertySignature(_)
349	            | TSSignature::TSMethodSignature(_)
350	            | TSSignature::TSIndexSignature(_)
351	            | TSSignature::TSConstructSignatureDeclaration(_) => None,
352	        })),
353	        TSType::TSTypeQuery(_)
354	        | TSType::TSBigIntKeyword(_)
355	        | TSType::TSBooleanKeyword(_)
356	        | TSType::TSIntrinsicKeyword(_)
357	        | TSType::TSNeverKeyword(_)
358	        | TSType::TSNullKeyword(_)
359	        | TSType::TSNumberKeyword(_)
360	        | TSType::TSObjectKeyword(_)
361	        | TSType::TSStringKeyword(_)
362	        | TSType::TSSymbolKeyword(_)
363	        | TSType::TSUndefinedKeyword(_)
364	        | TSType::TSVoidKeyword(_)
365	        | TSType::TSArrayType(_)
366	        | TSType::TSConditionalType(_)
367	        | TSType::TSConstructorType(_)

370	        | TSType::TSInferType(_)
371	        | TSType::TSIntersectionType(_)

387	/// The evidence of a type's call signatures, given their declared results (`None` when one declares none): see
388	/// [`combine`].
389	fn results<'a, 'b>(signatures: impl Iterator<Item = Option<&'b TSType<'a>>>) -> Evidence<'b, 'a> {
390	    combine(signatures.map(|result| match result.map(result_of) {
391	        Some(Returns::Neither) => Evidence::NotRenderable,
392	        Some(Returns::Node) => Evidence::NoComponent,
393	        Some(Returns::Empty | Returns::Maybe) | None => Evidence::Unknown,
394	    }))
395	}

397	/// The evidence of several signatures or declarations of one callee, each read alone: [`Evidence::NotRenderable`] when
398	/// every one is, [`Evidence::NoComponent`] when every one is that or `NotRenderable`, and [`Evidence::Unknown`]
399	/// otherwise or when there are none. One that may give a component keeps the whole callee a candidate.
400	fn combine<'a, 'b>(all: impl Iterator<Item = Evidence<'b, 'a>>) -> Evidence<'b, 'a> {
401	    let mut combined = None;
402	    for evidence in all {
403	        combined = Some(match (combined, evidence) {
404	            (None | Some(Evidence::NotRenderable), Evidence::NotRenderable) => Evidence::NotRenderable,
405	            (None | Some(Evidence::NotRenderable | Evidence::NoComponent), Evidence::NoComponent)
406	            | (Some(Evidence::NoComponent), Evidence::NotRenderable) => Evidence::NoComponent,
407	            (_, Evidence::Identity | Evidence::Reference(_) | Evidence::Unknown)
408	            | (
409	                Some(Evidence::Identity | Evidence::Reference(_) | Evidence::Unknown),
410	                Evidence::NoComponent | Evidence::NotRenderable,
411	            ) => return Evidence::Unknown,
412	        });
413	    }
414	    combined.unwrap_or(Evidence::Unknown)
415	}

417	/// What a call's declared result says about whether it is a component and whether React renders it.
418	#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
419	enum Returns {
420	    /// What React renders as a node and no component is: a string, number, bigint or boolean keyword, `void`, a
421	    /// literal or template literal, a type predicate, an array of those, or a union with one of them and nothing that
422	    /// may be a component.
423	    Node,
424	    /// Neither a component nor a node: the `object`, `symbol` and `never` keywords, an object type with no call or
425	    /// construct signature, an array of those or of `unknown`/`any` (TypeScript does not take `unknown` for a node).
426	    Neither,
427	    /// `null` or `undefined`: what a component may return, and no evidence alone.
428	    Empty,
429	    /// Anything that may be a component or an element, or that the extractor does not read (a reference, `unknown`).
430	    Maybe,
431	}
432	
433	fn result_of(ty: &TSType<'_>) -> Returns {
434	    match ty {
435	        TSType::TSBigIntKeyword(_)
436	        | TSType::TSBooleanKeyword(_)
437	        | TSType::TSNumberKeyword(_)
438	        | TSType::TSStringKeyword(_)
439	        | TSType::TSVoidKeyword(_)
440	        | TSType::TSLiteralType(_)
441	        | TSType::TSTemplateLiteralType(_)
442	        | TSType::TSTypePredicate(_) => Returns::Node,
443	        TSType::TSNeverKeyword(_) | TSType::TSObjectKeyword(_) | TSType::TSSymbolKeyword(_) => Returns::Neither,
444	        TSType::TSNullKeyword(_) | TSType::TSUndefinedKeyword(_) => Returns::Empty,
445	        TSType::TSParenthesizedType(inner) => result_of(&inner.type_annotation),
446	        TSType::TSTypeLiteral(literal) => {
447	            let callable = literal.members.iter().any(|signature| match signature {
448	                TSSignature::TSCallSignatureDeclaration(_) | TSSignature::TSConstructSignatureDeclaration(_) => true,
449	                TSSignature::TSPropertySignature(_)
450	                | TSSignature::TSMethodSignature(_)
451	                | TSSignature::TSIndexSignature(_) => false,
452	            });
453	            if callable { Returns::Maybe } else { Returns::Neither }
454	        }
455	        // `ReactNode[]` and `string[]` render; `unknown[]` does not.
456	        TSType::TSArrayType(array) => match (&array.element_type, result_of(&array.element_type)) {
457	            (TSType::TSAnyKeyword(_) | TSType::TSUnknownKeyword(_), _) => Returns::Neither,
458	            (_, Returns::Maybe) => Returns::Maybe,
459	            (_, Returns::Node | Returns::Empty) => Returns::Node,
460	            (_, Returns::Neither) => Returns::Neither,
461	        },
462	        // The value is one of the members: it may render when one does, and is a candidate when one may be.
463	        TSType::TSUnionType(union) => {
464	            let mut result = Returns::Empty;
465	            for member in &union.types {
466	                result = match (result, result_of(member)) {
467	                    (Returns::Maybe, _) | (_, Returns::Maybe) => return Returns::Maybe,
468	                    (Returns::Node, _) | (_, Returns::Node) => Returns::Node,
469	                    (Returns::Neither, _) | (_, Returns::Neither) => Returns::Neither,
470	                    (Returns::Empty, Returns::Empty) => Returns::Empty,
471	                };
472	            }
473	            result
474	        }
475	        TSType::TSAnyKeyword(_)
476	        | TSType::TSUnknownKeyword(_)
477	        | TSType::TSIntrinsicKeyword(_)
478	        | TSType::TSThisType(_)
479	        | TSType::TSConditionalType(_)
480	        | TSType::TSConstructorType(_)
481	        | TSType::TSFunctionType(_)
482	        | TSType::TSImportType(_)
483	        | TSType::TSIndexedAccessType(_)
484	        | TSType::TSInferType(_)
485	        | TSType::TSIntersectionType(_)
486	        | TSType::TSMappedType(_)
487	        | TSType::TSNamedTupleMember(_)
488	        | TSType::TSTupleType(_)
489	        | TSType::TSTypeOperatorType(_)
490	        | TSType::TSTypeQuery(_)
491	        | TSType::TSTypeReference(_)
492	        | TSType::JSDocNullableType(_)
493	        | TSType::JSDocNonNullableType(_)
494	        | TSType::JSDocUnknownType(_) => Returns::Maybe,
495	    }
496	}

498	/// Whether `typeof name` is the type of `expr`: the same identifier or the same chain of static members, read through
499	/// the namespaces' wrappers (the outermost assertion states the type whatever the namespace was asserted to).
500	fn query_names(name: &TSTypeQueryExprName<'_>, expr: &Expression<'_>) -> bool {
501	    match name {
502	        TSTypeQueryExprName::IdentifierReference(id) => matches!(expr, Expression::Identifier(e) if e.name == id.name),
503	        TSTypeQueryExprName::QualifiedName(qualified) => type_name_names(&qualified.left, &qualified.right, expr),
504	        TSTypeQueryExprName::ThisExpression(_) => matches!(expr, Expression::ThisExpression(_)),
505	        TSTypeQueryExprName::TSImportType(_) => false,
506	    }
507	}
508	
509	fn type_name_names(left: &TSTypeName<'_>, right: &IdentifierName<'_>, expr: &Expression<'_>) -> bool {
510	    let Expression::StaticMemberExpression(member) = expr else { return false };
511	    if member.property.name != right.name {
512	        return false;
513	    }
514	    let object = peel_expr(&member.object);
515	    match left {
516	        TSTypeName::IdentifierReference(id) => matches!(object, Expression::Identifier(e) if e.name == id.name),
517	        TSTypeName::QualifiedName(qualified) => type_name_names(&qualified.left, &qualified.right, object),
518	        TSTypeName::ThisExpression(_) => matches!(object, Expression::ThisExpression(_)),
519	    }
520	}
521	
522	/// Whether a dotted chain (`createButton`, `React.forwardRef`) names `expr`, read through the namespaces' wrappers.
523	fn chain_names(chain: &str, expr: &Expression<'_>) -> bool {
524	    match (chain.rsplit_once('.'), expr) {
525	        (None, Expression::Identifier(id)) => id.name == chain,
526	        (Some((left, right)), Expression::StaticMemberExpression(member)) => {
527	            member.property.name == right && chain_names(left, peel_expr(&member.object))
528	        }
529	        (None | Some(_), _) => false,
530	    }
531	}

591	/// The module-level aliases of a value's type, `type Factory = typeof createButton`, as alias name to the dotted chain
592	/// it queries. Only a name the file declares once in type space is kept: an import, an interface merged with it, a
593	/// type parameter or a namespace's own type of that name may be what a use means, and which one is not read here.
594	pub(super) fn typeof_aliases(program: &Program<'_>) -> FxHashMap<CompactString, CompactString> {
595	    fn chain(name: &TSTypeName<'_>) -> Option<String> {
596	        match name {
597	            TSTypeName::IdentifierReference(id) => Some(id.name.as_str().to_owned()),
598	            TSTypeName::QualifiedName(qualified) => {
599	                Some(format!("{}.{}", chain(&qualified.left)?, qualified.right.name))
600	            }
601	            TSTypeName::ThisExpression(_) => None,
602	        }
603	    }
604	    let mut declared = TypeNames::default();
605	    oxc_ast_visit::Visit::visit_program(&mut declared, program);
606	    let mut aliases = FxHashMap::default();
607	    for statement in &program.body {
608	        let declaration = match statement {
609	            Statement::ExportDeclaration(export) => Some(&export.declaration),
610	            _ => statement.as_declaration(),
611	        };
612	        let Some(Declaration::TSTypeAliasDeclaration(declaration)) = declaration else { continue };
613	        let mut ty = &declaration.type_annotation;
614	        while let TSType::TSParenthesizedType(inner) = ty {
615	            ty = &inner.type_annotation;
616	        }
617	        let queried = match ty {
618	            TSType::TSTypeQuery(query) if declaration.type_parameters.is_none() && query.type_arguments.is_none() => {
619	                match &query.expr_name {
620	                    TSTypeQueryExprName::IdentifierReference(id) => Some(id.name.as_str().to_owned()),
621	                    TSTypeQueryExprName::QualifiedName(qualified) => {
622	                        chain(&qualified.left).map(|left| format!("{left}.{}", qualified.right.name))
623	                    }
624	                    TSTypeQueryExprName::ThisExpression(_) | TSTypeQueryExprName::TSImportType(_) => None,
625	                }
626	            }
627	            _ => None,
628	        };
629	        if let Some(queried) = queried
630	            && declared.0.get(declaration.id.name.as_str()) == Some(&1)
631	        {
632	            aliases.insert(CompactString::from(declaration.id.name.as_str()), CompactString::from(queried));
633	        }
634	    }
635	    aliases
636	}

Exit code 1
## What

Bumps the oxc crates 0.158 -> 0.159 (dependabot) and fixes the two detection regressions the bump caused, at the class level.

**What changed in OXC 0.159** (diff of `oxc_ast` and `oxc_parser` 0.158.0 vs 0.159.0 in the cargo registry):

- `oxc_parser` now splits an instantiation's type arguments onto the enclosing node only when the instantiation is unparenthesized (`split_unparenthesized_instantiation`, "as in TypeScript"). 0.158 split it whatever the parentheses. Under our `preserve_parens: false` this changes four shapes:
  - call: `(f<T>)(x)` is now `CallExpression { callee: TSInstantiationExpression(f, T), type_arguments: None }` (was `callee: f, type_arguments: T`)
  - heritage: `class C extends (B<T>)` is now `heritage.expression: TSInstantiationExpression(B, T)`, `heritage.type_arguments: None`
  - `new (A<T>)()`: `new.callee` is a `TSInstantiationExpression`
  - tagged template `(f<T>)`...``: `tag` is a `TSInstantiationExpression`
- `oxc_ast`: the only type change is a new `label_id` field on `LabelIdentifier` (labels; not read by us).
- Parser behaviour with no effect on what we read: a string followed by an operator or member access is no longer a directive; `as`/`satisfies` before `**` stops the expression; numeric-separator diagnostics; lexer and checkpoint refactors. `ParseOptions`/`preserve_parens` unchanged.

**A component is found when its `forwardRef`, `memo` or base class is wrapped in parentheses, a cast or type arguments.** `export const Button = (React.forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, Props>)((props, ref) => …)` and `class Button extends (React.Component<Props>) {}` list their props, where they were skipped.

- Why it matters: libraries write these forms to satisfy their own typing, and a skipped component shows no Controls.
- Covered: parentheses, `as`, `satisfies`, `!` and type arguments, around the callee or the base class, in `.ts` and `.tsx`.
- Also covered: a generic component given type arguments where it is wrapped or aliased, such as `memo(List<Row>)`, `Object.assign(List<Row>, { Item })` or `const RowList = List<Row>`, with or without a cast or `!` around it.
  - Limit: the props are the generic component's own (`ListProps<T>`); the type arguments are not applied to them.
- Nothing to adopt: output for components that were already found is unchanged.
- Limit: a cast drops a component only when it says the call returns no component or element. `(memo as (c: unknown) => object)(…)`, and casts whose result is a string, number, `void`, a literal or an array of `unknown`, are not listed. Every other cast, such as `(forwardRef as forwardRefType)(…)` or a callable type returning `React.FC<Props>`, is read as the plain call.
  - A component that returns another component's result, `return (Greeting as (p: Props) => string)(props)`, is still found: a component may return a string, number or `null`. Only a cast whose result React cannot render, such as `object`, drops it.
- Limit: only a cast to the callee's own type (`typeof` the callee, a `type Factory = typeof createButton` alias, `any` or `unknown`) keeps the callee's declaration. A generic wrapper cast to another signature gets the props of its render function, not the extra props its own declaration adds, and a factory cast that way (`(createButton as SomeFactory)()`) is not listed.
  - An alias counts only when the file declares its name once as a type: a factory cast to an alias that is also imported, declared in a namespace, merged with an interface or reused as a type parameter is not listed.

## Review round 6 (code review of fbd83a0d; fixed in 33b492b9)

**Root cause.** Findings 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are the same class as rounds 4 and 5: a verdict taken from something that is not evidence. A dropped instantiation read as "no type arguments", an unrelated declaration read as "ambiguous here", `never` and a setter read as "no component", a string-returning factory read as "renders". Each fix below decides from what the source says at the site and leaves unknown as unknown. Sibling readers of `Peeled`, `named()`, `renderable()` and `peel_expr` were swept for each.

**Findings:**
- 1 CONFIRMED, fixed. `alias_shape` reads the aliased value with `instantiated()` (`No` / `Given` / `Unread`). `finish()` gives every mapping the type parameters of the functions it spans, and then `bind_alias_instantiations` binds them in the props type's arguments. `memo(List<Row>)`, `withTheme(List<Row>)`, `Object.assign(List<Row>, { Item })` and `const RowList = List<Row>` (also parenthesised, `!`, `satisfies`, `as any` above it) list `ListProps<Row>` with no type parameters left. Some arguments cannot be bound: a count other than the parameters', a parameter used inside a props argument (`GridProps<T[]>`), a cast beneath the instantiation (`(List as any)<Row>`), or two instantiations. Then the props stay `ListProps<T>` and one `GENERIC_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH` warning (the existing code for unfilled type parameters) names the alias, its component and the reason. The imported sibling (`const RowList = ImportedList<Row>`, read as `ComponentProps<typeof ImportedList>`, which cannot carry arguments) emits the same warning. Attachments (`Root.Item = Item<Row>`) export the same component under a path and make no new candidate, so they are unchanged. Tests: `an_instantiated_component_binds_its_type_parameters_or_says_it_did_not` (4 sites x 5 bound forms with exact mappings, 4 sites x 2 unbound forms with one warning each, the nested-parameter warning text) and `an_instantiated_imported_component_says_its_type_arguments_are_not_applied`. Both fail on fbd83a0d.
- 2 CONFIRMED, fixed. `typeof_aliases` first scans the top-level statements for `type X = typeof y`. That scan allocates nothing unless one is found. With no candidate it returns before any walk. With one, it counts the top-level type-space declarations of the candidate names (imports, type aliases, interfaces, classes, enums, namespaces, `import =`) by a loop over `program.body`, and runs one walk (`Shadows`) that compares names against the candidates by `&str`, allocating nothing per name. That walk skips every `TSType`, since a type holds no expression. Test `only_a_module_with_a_typeof_alias_is_walked_for_shadowing_names`: with a step counter, a module with type parameters and a mapped type but no alias is walked 0 times, and one with an alias once. Instructions retired, Chakra (`extract --src chakra-ui/packages/react/src --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies --json`), release builds, 5 runs interleaved, `/usr/bin/time -l` (load average 30 to 43):
  - `--no-checker`: fbd83a0d median 21.92 G (range 21.67 to 22.22 G); this head median 21.98 G (21.75 to 22.07 G, plus one outlier at 29.84 G). That is +0.28%, inside the run-to-run spread.
  - with the checker: fbd83a0d median 87.17 G (87.15 to 95.29 G); this head median 88.21 G (87.34 to 88.43 G). That is +1.19%, inside the spread.
  - So the removed walk is below what a whole-run count resolves on Chakra: no measurable win or loss. What the change guarantees is the 0 walks the counter test shows.
- 3 CONFIRMED, fixed. Only the module's own top-level type-space declarations count toward "declared once". An inner declaration of the name (a type parameter of a function, arrow or class, including methods; a type alias, interface, class, enum or namespace inside a namespace, function, block or class; a class expression's own name) records its scope's span. `TypeofAlias::means_at(span)` declines the alias for a cast inside such a scope, so the cast's evidence is `Unknown`. Type parameters of types, mapped keys and `infer` hold no expression, so they never shadow a cast. Declined at the module level, the factory form gets the existing `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` ("'Button' is a PascalCase binding but matched no known component pattern …"), asserted in the test. A generic HOC call whose callee is declined (`wrapper_callee`) has no diagnostic of its own. None exists for "the callee's declaration was not read", and none was added. Tests: `a_typeof_alias_is_shadowed_only_where_its_name_is_declared_again` (11 unrelated declarations keep the alias, among them a type parameter elsewhere, a mapped key, `infer`, a nested namespace, `declare module` and a block-local type; 7 module-level ones decline it with the skip) and `a_redeclaration_around_the_cast_shadows_the_alias` (14 rows over `means_at`: function, arrow, class, method type parameters around the cast; a namespace or function-local declaration around it; a class expression's name; the same declarations elsewhere). The first fails on fbd83a0d; the second uses the new API.
- 4 CONFIRMED, fixed. `never` is now `Returns::Maybe`, so `Unknown`, like `any` and `unknown`. In a union it adds nothing (`string | never` is `string`, still `NoComponent`). Test `a_never_result_is_no_evidence_against_a_call`: `named()` (`(memo as (c: any) => never)`, a callable literal), a namespace member typed `=> never`, and `renderable()` (`return (Greeting as (p: Props) => never)(props)`) all keep the plain result, and `string | never` still declines. Fails on fbd83a0d. Hook reader: see 7.
- 5 CONFIRMED, fixed. A setter is no declaration the call can reach: `declarations()` drops it. So getter plus setter reads as the getter alone. `{ get forwardRef(): (...a) => object; set forwardRef(v) }` and the method-plus-setter row are `NotRenderable` and decline. An untyped property, method or getter that could answer the call stays `Unknown` through `combine`. The rule: `NotRenderable` only when every declaration that could answer the call is read and non-renderable.
